subcommittees.name: Public Lands, Forests, and Mining Subcommittee

dimensions.assessment: Affects governing bodies and community users of 27 recognized community land grants-mercedes in New Mexico, federal land management agencies, and consulted Indian Tribes.
dimensions.evidence: greater cooperation and coordination between the Federal Government and the governing bodies and community users of land grant-mercedes in New Mexico

dimensions.assessment: Establishes formal administrative frameworks, coordination processes, fee reduction considerations, and evaluation sections in land use plans for historical and traditional uses.
dimensions.evidence: provide for enhanced cooperation and coordination between the Secretary concerned and qualified land grant-mercedes

dimensions.assessment: Directs consideration of fee reductions or waivers based on socioeconomic conditions and operating budgets, but specifies no federal spending amounts.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary concerned is authorized to reduce or waive land use fees or consider the fiscal capacity of the applicant

dimensions.assessment: Applies specific procedural, consultative, and land-use planning requirements to federal public lands under the BLM and Forest Service within New Mexico.
dimensions.evidence: In developing, maintaining, and revising land use plans... include a section in the applicable land use plan that considers and evaluates the impact of other uses

dimensions.assessment: Requires an initial MOU within 2 years, ongoing renewals or extensions, and permanent integration into land use planning revisions.
dimensions.evidence: not later than 2 years after the date of enactment of this Act, enter into an initial memorandum of understanding

missing_information: Fiscal estimates or administrative cost projections for executing the memorandum of understanding and updating land use plans.
importance_detail.rationale: Directs the BLM and Forest Service to enter into a memorandum of understanding with the New Mexico Land Grant Council concerning historical and traditional uses of federal public lands by qualified land grants-mercedes in New Mexico.
